name: Casa Gaspar
key_features: White walled square closed to the outside; a higher central band opens to two courtyards with a pool.

name: Villa Busk
key_features: A 40 m concrete and timber wing on bedrock, linked by a glazed bridge to a four-storey tower with a pyramid roof.

name: Los Manantiales Restaurant
key_features: Four intersecting hyperbolic paraboloids form an eight-lobed concrete shell only centimetres thick.

name: Meiso no Mori Municipal Funeral Hall
key_features: Thin white concrete roof that rises and falls like a cloud, resting on tapered columns beside a pond.

name: Casa Rotonda
key_features: Three-level cylindrical house split north–south by a cut that brings daylight down from the roof.

name: Villa Schreiner
key_features: Low timber house on a modular grid, with Japanese-influenced post-and-beam structure and sliding walls.

name: Marie Short House
key_features: Two near-identical timber pavilions on stilts under curved corrugated metal roofs; louvres adjust air and light.

name: Hillside Terrace
key_features: Low mixed-use blocks built in phases along a street, with small courts and passages open to the sidewalk.

name: Casa Rustici
key_features: Two parallel slabs tied across the street front by thin balcony frames, leaving an open court between.

name: House in White
key_features: Square white house under a pyramidal roof, with a single cedar column standing in the main room.

name: Paper House
key_features: 110 paper tubes, 2.7 m tall, stand in an S-curve under a flat roof; the first building to use paper tubes as structure.

name: Café De Unie
key_features: De Stijl facade of primary-coloured planes and lettering, rebuilt on a new site after its wartime loss.

name: Hubertus House
key_features: A rainbow-coloured steel and glass infill for single parents, stepping in among old street houses.

name: House N
key_features: Three boxes nested inside each other, each wall cut with big openings, so garden and house blur into layers.

name: 25 bis rue Franklin
key_features: A concrete frame shown on the facade, filled with floral ceramic tiles, set around a U-shaped recessed front.

name: Centro de Artes de Sines
key_features: Stone-clad blocks on both sides of a street, linked below ground; a glazed base opens to the pavement.

name: Collegio del Colle
key_features: Student rooms in brick-and-concrete terraces that step down the hillside facing Urbino.

name: Nantes School of Architecture
key_features: Concrete frame with extra-high floors linked by a ramp, leaving open unprogrammed spaces and a rooftop.

name: Casa Gilardi
key_features: Indoor pool with a freestanding red column, lit through a yellow-glazed corridor.

name: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport Terminal 1
key_features: Round concrete drum crossed by glass-tube escalators, linked by tunnels to seven satellite gates.

name: Rabindra Bhavan
key_features: Home of three national arts academies: a Y-shaped four-storey block shaded by rows of concrete sunshades.

name: École de plein air de Suresnes
key_features: Open-air school against tuberculosis: eight classroom pavilions whose glazed walls fold open, on Mont-Valérien.

name: CEPT University
key_features: An architecture school of brick and concrete, open to the campus at every level.

name: Church on the Wind
key_features: A long frosted-glass colonnade leads to a concrete chapel framing a view of the hillside.

name: Quinta da Malagueira
key_features: About 1,200 white courtyard row houses, served by a raised concrete 'aqueduct' carrying water and power.

name: Santa Maria da Feira Municipal Market
key_features: Butterfly-roofed concrete stalls stepping down a sloping site around an open courtyard.

name: Pousada Santa Maria do Bouro
key_features: A ruined monastery made into a hotel: the stone walls are kept, with flat new roofs and frameless glass set inside.

name: Central Saint Martins, Granary Building
key_features: An 1850s granary and its sheds turned into an art school, joined by a long top-lit internal street.

name: Diagoon Houses
key_features: Split-level 'unfinished' houses of two cores and half-floors that residents can enclose and extend.

name: University of Ruhuna
key_features: Pavilions with tiled roofs linked by covered walkways across hilltops overlooking the sea.

name: Minna no Mori Gifu Media Cosmos
key_features: An undulating cypress lattice roof with fabric globes that draw in daylight and exhaust warm air.

name: Dominus Winery
key_features: Long low box walled in gabions of local basalt, which shade the cellars and let light filter through.

name: Dutch Pavilion, Venice Biennale
key_features: A plain cubic gallery in the Giardini, lit by high clerestory windows in its raised centre.

name: Gunma Music Center
key_features: Thin folded-plate concrete roof and walls zigzag over the hall, funded partly by citizens' donations.

name: Centre for Development Studies
key_features: Rat-trap bond and perforated brick jalis: cheap, cool and built by local masons.

name: Cosmic Rays Pavilion
key_features: Twin hyperbolic-paraboloid shells so thin they let cosmic rays through to the instruments.

name: Vertical Courtyard Apartments
key_features: Housing towers with two-storey courtyards stacked into the facade, giving each flat a garden in the air.

name: Atelier Bardill
key_features: Red-brown concrete studio around a courtyard open to the sky through a large oval hole.

name: Naoshima Ferry Terminal
key_features: A thin flat roof on slender steel columns covers glass boxes and an open waiting space by the quay.

name: Bacardi Bottling Plant
key_features: Roof of three square groined vaults, each two intersecting hyperbolic paraboloids, 4 cm thick at the edges.

name: Capilla del Retiro
key_features: Chapel set down into the ground below a lattice of laminated timber beams and glass, open to the Andes.

name: Casa Papanice
key_features: Curving walls and a ribbed facade of coloured ceramic-tube 'organ pipes' spread out from the corners.

name: Gartenstadt Falkenberg
key_features: Garden city terraces painted in strong colours, nicknamed the paintbox estate.

name: Paks Catholic Church
key_features: Timber-framed church with a shingled roof and three spires, its form drawn from Hungarian folk motifs.

name: ATIRA (Ahmedabad Textile Industry's Research Association)
key_features: One of independent India's first modernist research campuses: a crisp framed lab block with long window bands.

name: Glass House, Seopjikoji
key_features: A V-shaped concrete-and-glass mass on the headland, opening east to Seongsan Ilchulbong.

name: Le Fresnoy
key_features: A great roof over the old 1920s leisure halls; the 'in-between' space under it holds catwalks and stairs.

name: Stegastein Viewpoint
key_features: A 30 m pine-and-steel walkway that leaps out from the hillside and stops in mid-air over the Aurlandsfjord.

name: Torres Blancas
key_features: Concrete tower of clustered cylinders with rounded cantilevered terraces and planted balconies.

name: Curtain Wall House
key_features: A two-storey fabric curtain stands in for the outside wall; drawn back, the living floor opens to the city.

name: St. Johann von Capistran
key_features: A round brick church whose flat roof rests on slim columns, with a large skylight over the altar.

name: Centennial Hall, Tokyo Institute of Technology
key_features: A half-cylinder of aluminium cuts diagonally across stacked boxes above a glazed hall.

name: Engel House
key_features: The first building in Tel Aviv lifted on pilotis, freeing the ground for shade and breeze on Rothschild Boulevard.

name: Fujisawa Municipal Gymnasium (Akibadai)
key_features: Two arenas under curved stainless-steel roofs, likened to a samurai helmet or a beetle.

name: Lister County Courthouse
key_features: Ochre Nordic-classical courthouse with a clock gable and a great arched, fan-glazed entrance.

name: Bordeaux Law Courts
key_features: Cedar-clad courtroom pods shaped like wine vats stand under an undulating roof behind a glass wall.

name: Japan Pavilion, Expo 2000
key_features: A long gridshell of paper tubes under a paper membrane roof, designed to be recycled afterwards.

name: Caja Granada Headquarters
key_features: Concrete cube with a deep gridded sunscreen facade; inside, a vast hall caught by skylights.

name: Church of Saint Anthony of Polana
key_features: Concrete church whose crown of tapering ribs rises to a point, with coloured glass set between them.

name: The Economist Building
key_features: Three buildings of different heights round a raised plaza off St James's Street, clad in Portland stone.

name: Cabanon de Le Corbusier
key_features: A single Modulor-proportioned room inside a log-clad hut on the coast.

name: Church of La Medalla Milagrosa
key_features: Thin hyperbolic paraboloid shells twist into columns and roof as one continuous concrete structure.

name: Bouça Social Housing
key_features: Parallel rows of stacked duplex homes with outside stairs and galleries, shielded from the railway by a long wall.

name: Sakaide Artificial Ground
key_features: A concrete deck 6 to 9 m up carries public housing and a new ground; shops, halls and parking sit beneath.

name: Aranya Low Cost Housing
key_features: Plots and a service core for 80,000 people, which families extend over time.

name: El Colegio de México
by: Teodoro González de León, Abraham Zabludovsky
key_features: Bush-hammered concrete blocks with marble chips stepping around a large terraced courtyard.

name: Les Orgues de Flandre
key_features: Housing towers that step up and down like organ pipes, named after musical forms.

name: Second Artigas House (Residência Vilanova Artigas II)
key_features: Artigas's own house of 1949, built before his concrete houses of the São Paulo school.

name: Casa De Blas
key_features: A light white steel table with a glass box beneath, set on a heavy concrete podium on a hilltop.

name: Bolgatanga Library
key_features: A raised, wing-like roof and perforated block walls let breezes and filtered light into the reading rooms.

name: Banco Borges & Irmão
key_features: Small white bank on a corner, its curved wall turning the street; the first Mies van der Rohe Award.

name: Arquipélago Contemporary Arts Centre
by: Menos é Mais Arquitectos, João Mendes Ribeiro
key_features: An 1890s basalt distillery restored and joined by two new concrete buildings for art and performance.

name: Chassé Theater
key_features: A single undulating roof sweeps over fly towers and foyers, gathering several halls into one form.

name: Marl Town Hall
key_features: Germany's first suspended towers: floors hung from the top of concrete cores, beside a council hall with a folded roof.

name: Murcia Town Hall Extension
key_features: Sandstone facade of irregular piers and openings, like a musical score, facing the cathedral square.

name: Asilo Sant'Elia
key_features: Kindergarten around a courtyard, its glazed classrooms shaded by a free concrete frame with awnings.

name: Auditorium Niccolò Paganini
key_features: A disused sugar factory shell opened with glass end walls so the concert hall looks out onto the park.

name: Burgo Tower
key_features: Office tower wrapped in a grid of metal bands that reads differently on each face, beside a low block.

name: Casa alle Zattere
key_features: A modern house on the Giudecca canal that reworks the Venetian palazzo: plaster walls, framed windows.

name: Casa das Mudas Art Centre
key_features: Dark basalt volumes set into a cliff top above the sea, with roof terraces and paths through the building.

name: DeFlat Kleiburg
key_features: A 1970s Bijlmermeer slab of 500 flats saved from demolition; residents buy bare shells and fit them out.

name: Lamune Onsen
key_features: Bathhouse of charred cedar and plaster, with pine trees sprouting from its rooftop towers.

name: Flower Tower
key_features: Ten storeys wrapped in balconies lined with about 380 concrete pots of bamboo, watered automatically.

name: Toyo Ito Museum of Architecture
key_features: Polyhedral steel hut and a rebuilt light-vaulted house sit on a slope above the Seto Inland Sea.

name: Bankinter Building
key_features: A sharp-edged brick office block rises behind a preserved 19th-century mansion, with deep-set windows.

name: Casa Planells
key_features: A narrow corner block on the Diagonal whose curved facade and wavy balconies turn the corner.

name: Centraal Beheer
key_features: Grid of concrete-block office islands linked by bridges across top-lit voids, left for users to fit out.

name: Siida
key_features: Home to the Sámi Museum and Northern Lapland Nature Centre, on Lake Inari; opened in 1998.

name: Teletón Children's Rehabilitation Centre
key_features: Prefabricated triangular panels of brick lattice fold into screens and spans that filter light.

name: Villa Gans
key_features: A protected grand residence above Kronberg im Taunus, by Peter Behrens with Camillo Karl Schneider.

name: Delta Shelter
key_features: Steel-clad cabin on four steel columns above a flood plain; four 10 by 18 ft steel shutters roll across to close it up.

name: Diar es Saâda
key_features: Load-bearing cut-stone housing blocks stepped down a hillside around public squares.

name: Edificio Basurto
key_features: Streamline apartment tower in Condesa with rounded balconies and a celebrated snail-shell spiral stair.

name: Bloco das Águas Livres
by: Nuno Teotónio Pereira and Bartolomeu Costa Cabral
key_features: Housing block with roof studios under half-vaults for north light, and integrated art incl. Almada Negreiros.

name: CapitaSpring
key_features: Tower of vertical fins that part at mid-height around a spiralling open-air garden.

name: Fukuoka Art Museum
key_features: Brick-red fired tiles cast into the concrete walls give a weathering skin facing Ohori Park.

name: Hohenhof
key_features: A total work of art: house, garden, furniture and fittings designed together for Karl Ernst Osthaus.

name: Unidad Vecinal Portales
key_features: Housing blocks linked by elevated walkways and bridges over shared gardens.

name: Usera Public Library (José Hierro)
key_features: Compact square tower of reading floors in grey cladding, with large framed windows looking over the park.

name: Academy of Arts, Hanseatenweg
key_features: Linked exhibition halls, studio block and a hall under a sweeping copper roof sit low in a park.

name: Asahi Group Oyamazaki Villa Museum of Art
key_features: A buried concrete cylinder gallery is reached by a stair from an older English-style hillside villa.

name: Burkina Institute of Technology
key_features: Long classroom blocks of cast earth walls under a raised metal roof that lets heat escape.

name: Acropolis and Philopappou Hill Paths
key_features: Paths paved with reused marble and stone fragments in irregular patterns, framing views of the Acropolis.

name: Bandung Institute of Technology (Aula Barat and Aula Timur)
key_features: Designed 1918, opened 1920; blends Indonesian vernacular architecture with modern elements.

name: Bruder Klaus Field Chapel
key_features: Concrete rammed around a tent of tree trunks, then burned out to leave a charred interior.

name: Das Gelbe Haus
key_features: Old village house stripped to its stone walls, painted white, with a new roof and one central timber column inside.

name: National Museum of the Republic
key_features: A white concrete dome sits on the open esplanade, entered by a ramp curling out from its side.

name: Termas Geométricas
key_features: A red timber walkway threads along a forested ravine, linking a chain of hot-spring pools and huts.

name: Cedar Rock (Lowell Walter House)
key_features: Usonian tadpole plan of brick, walnut and glass; glass-walled living room faces the river; no basement or attic.

name: St. Anna, Düren
key_features: L-shaped church whose walls are built from the rubble stone of the bombed medieval church.

name: Venezuela Pavilion, Venice Biennale
key_features: Small national pavilion in the Giardini designed by Carlo Scarpa in 1954-56.

name: Yatsushiro Municipal Museum
key_features: Galleries hidden under a grassy mound; above, light billowing roofs and a floating half-cylinder store.

name: Academy of Arts, Pariser Platz
by: Günter Behnisch with Werner Durth (Behnisch & Partner)
key_features: An all-glass front on Pariser Platz, defying the square's design rules, opening onto the old academy halls behind.

name: Azerbaijan Carpet Museum
key_features: A long building shaped like a partly rolled carpet, its metal cladding patterned like weaving.

name: Bagno Pubblico, Bellinzona
by: Aurelio Galfetti, Flora Ruchat-Roncati and Ivo Trümpy
key_features: Public pools organised along one long walkway that runs from the town to the Ticino riverbank.

name: Government House, Yerevan
key_features: Tamanian's north-west wing built 1926-29; his son Gevorg finished the rest by 1941.

name: Za-Koenji Public Theatre
key_features: Tent-like dark steel-plate concrete shell, its roof carved by cones and cylinders, pricked with small glazed portholes.

name: Osaka International Convention Center (Grand Cube Osaka)
key_features: Convention centre in Osaka with its own underground station on the Keihan Nakanoshima line.

name: Library and Learning Center, Vienna University of Economics
key_features: Walls leaning at 35 degrees and a massive black volume cantilevered at an angle over the campus plaza.

name: Biblioteca cantonale, Lugano
key_features: Ticino's key modernist work, in Parco Ciani: an L-plan library with a windowless, Bauhaus-inspired book-stack wing.

name: Open Chapel of Lomas de Cuernavaca (Palmira Chapel)
by: Félix Candela, with Guillermo Rosell and Manuel Larrosa
key_features: A single 4 cm hyperbolic-paraboloid saddle that opens 30 m wide at the front and rises to a 21 m point.

name: Chiesa Madre di Gibellina
key_features: A great white sphere set on a cubic block, built in the new town after the 1968 Belice earthquake.

name: Cinémathèque française (former American Center)
key_features: Stone-clad block whose park side breaks into tilting, folding forms under a curling zinc roof.

name: Museum Liner (Kunstmuseum Appenzell)
key_features: Galleries under a saw-tooth of gables of varying height, roof and walls clad in overlapping stainless-steel sheets.

name: SDU Campus Kolding
key_features: Triangular university building wrapped in perforated steel shutters that open and close with the daylight.

name: AaltoAlvari swimming hall
key_features: Alvar Aalto's swimming hall on Seminaarinmäki in Jyväskylä, before its later extension.

name: Amsterdam Orphanage (Burgerweeshuis)
key_features: Repeated domed units clustered along diagonal internal streets make the orphanage a small city.

name: Appleby Blue Almshouse
key_features: Almshouse flats for older people in brick ranges round a planted courtyard, reached by shared timber-lined galleries.

name: Archaeological Museum of Ioannina
key_features: Concrete frame filled with local stone, low pavilions round a courtyard in a park.

name: Bensberg Town Hall
key_features: Concrete town hall built into a medieval castle's ruins, crowned by a jagged stair tower.
